title: No way to take the backoff delay from the failure itself
text_original: Just a small feature I frequently use with HTTP requests, in case you are interested.
text_rewritten: When a server answers 429 it tells us exactly how long to wait; when it answers 503 we want our own, longer pause. Today every wait strategy derives the delay from the attempt number or from a constant, so the only way to honour what the server told us is to write a raw callable and rediscover how to pull the exception out of the retry state — and every one of our services has now done that slightly differently, with slightly different bugs. Please add a public wait strategy named `wait_exception(predicate)`, exported from the package root, where `predicate` receives the exception that was raised and returns the number of seconds to pause before the next attempt. All the existing wait strategies must be left untouched.

Today every wait strategy derives the delay from the attempt number or from a constant, so the only way to honour what the server told us is to write a raw callable and rediscover how to pull the exception out of the retry state — and every one of our services has now done that slightly differently, with slightly different bugs. Please add a public wait strategy named `wait_exception(predicate)`, exported from the package root, where `predicate` receives the exception that was raised and returns the number of seconds to pause before the next attempt. All the existing wait strategies must be left untouched.
acceptance_hint: `wait_exception(predicate)` calls the predicate once per failed attempt, hands it the raised exception, and uses the number it returns as that attempt's pause; chained and fixed waits behave exactly as before.
